sanitization: Real Devin CLI 3000.6.14 hook stdin captured via a capture-only .devin/hooks.v1.json logger on Linux/WSL2. Only paths, session/prompt/tool-use/agent identifiers, shell ids, and verbose prompt text were replaced with placeholders. Property names, nesting, booleans, missing-vs-null distinctions, response status, and correlation relationships are preserved exactly. No secrets, no real document content, no unredacted user prompts.

placeholderLegend.<session>: real session_id is a short human-readable slug (e.g. 'bramble-scorpion'), NOT a UUID
placeholderLegend.<prompt-id>: real prompt_id is a UUID v4, rotated per user prompt; ABSENT on SessionStart (fires before first prompt)
placeholderLegend.<tool-use-id-child>: subagent tool_use_id format: 'functions.<tool>:<n>' (observed on subagent-issued reads/greps/globs)
placeholderLegend.<project-root>: absolute path of the capture fixture project root
placeholderLegend.<agent-id>: 8-char hex subagent identifier (e.g. '7f4c7180'), embedded in run_subagent/read_subagent output strings and read_subagent tool_input
placeholderLegend.<shell-id>: short hex shell id embedded in exec PostToolUse output

C01.scenario: Session start, then an ordinary human prompt (devin -p, minimal reply).

C10.scenario: End the fixture session normally (devin -p exits after replying).
notes: SessionEnd DOES fire on 3000.6.14 (the 3000.5.20 changelog fix).
reason observed value is 'other' for a normal -p exit.
No cwd, no transcript_path on SessionEnd.
prompt_id IS present on SessionEnd (the session saw at least one user prompt).

C02_read.scenario: Harmless read of a sentinel file.
fieldObservations: read tool_input: {file_path, limit?}. limit is OPTIONAL (omitted in another capture).
tool_response is an OBJECT {success:boolean, output:string, error:string|null} — NOT a bare string.
tool_input is echoed verbatim in PostToolUse.
tool_use_id correlates Pre and Post.
glob tool_input: {pattern, path?}. path is the search root; OPTIONAL (omitted in subagent-issued glob, see C09).

tool_response.output:
Found <n> match(es) for pattern 'searchable' in <project-root>:
-- <matches summary>

fieldObservations: grep tool_input: {pattern, path?, glob_pattern?}. path is OPTIONAL (defaults to project root).
A grep content 'pattern' is NOT a file path; the core path checker must not scan it.

C02_grep_globPattern.scenario: Content grep WITH a glob_pattern file filter (issued by a subagent — see C09 for identity).

tool_response.output: No matches found for pattern 'searchable' in <project-root>

fieldObservations: CONFIRMED: Devin grep exposes the content-search file filter as 'glob_pattern' (NOT 'glob'). The core reviewer-scope path checker inspects 'glob'; normalization is required for S07.
When glob_pattern is set and path is omitted, the search root defaults to the project root (visible in the output string).
notebook_read tool_input: {notebook_path}. The core reviewer-scope checker must forward 'notebook_path' (NOT 'file_path').

C02_exec.scenario: Harmless exec of an echo command.

tool_response.output:
Output from command in shell <shell-id>:
capture-exec-probe


Exit code: 0

fieldObservations: exec tool_input: {command, ...}. Additional fields (shell_id, timeout, workdir, env, tty) observed in the tool schema are optional and not present in this minimal call.

C03_write.scenario: Harmless write of a new sentinel file (auto-approved via --permission-mode accept-edits).
fieldObservations: write tool_input: {file_path, content}.
A rejected write (default --permission-mode auto in -p headless) fires PreToolUse but NO PostToolUse — the tool is rejected before execution. See C03_rejectedWrite.

C03_edit.scenario: Harmless edit of an existing sentinel file.

tool_response.output:
The file <project-root>/src/notes.md has been updated. Here's the result of running `cat -n` on a snippet of the edited file:
  1|# Captured Notes
  2|A harmless notebook-style markdown file.

fieldObservations: edit tool_input: {file_path, old_string, new_string}.

C03_rejectedWrite.scenario: A write rejected by the default 'auto' permission mode in headless -p (no human to confirm).
fieldObservations: ONLY PreToolUse fires for a rejected tool; NO PostToolUse. The agent sees a stderr warning 'rejected a tool call that requires confirmation'.
Implication for S08: a failed/canceled ask_user_question likewise fires PreToolUse but NOT PostToolUse (see C07_cancel). A PostToolUse response must NOT be mined from a tool that never executed.

C04_foregroundSubagent.scenario: Foreground run_subagent dispatch with a profile; subagent does a read; parent waits and reports.

tool_input.task: <prompt: read sentinel and report first line>
tool_input.title: Read sentinel.txt first line

tool_input.task: <prompt: read sentinel and report first line>
tool_input.title: Read sentinel.txt first line

tool_response.output:
Subagent agent_id=<agent-id> completed successfully:

<subagent report text>

fieldObservations: run_subagent tool_input (foreground): {profile, task, title?}. NO is_background field when foreground (field ABSENT, not false).

The child subagent's tool calls (read/glob/grep) fire as separate PreToolUse/PostToolUse events sharing the PARENT session_id and prompt_id. There is NO child session_id, NO profile, NO agent_type, NO agent_id field on the child tool events.
The child's agent_id appears ONLY embedded inside the parent's run_subagent PostToolUse output STRING ('Subagent agent_id=<agent-id> completed successfully:'). It is NOT a structured field.
Child tool_use_id uses a different format ('functions.<tool>:<n>') than parent ('chatcmpl-tool-<hex>'), but this is not a documented identity contract.

C05_backgroundLaunch.scenario: Background run_subagent dispatch (is_background:true); parent launches and stops without waiting.

tool_input.title: Read sentinel file
tool_input.task: <prompt: read sentinel and report first line>

tool_input.title: Read sentinel file
tool_input.task: <prompt: read sentinel and report first line>

tool_response.output: Background subagent started with agent_id=<agent-id>. You can wait for this agent to finish using the read_subagent tool, otherwise you will automatically be notified with a <subagent_completion_notification> when it completes.

fieldObservations: run_subagent tool_input (background): {profile, task, title?, is_background:true}. is_background is a BOOLEAN.
The launch acknowledgment is a PostToolUse with success:true; the agent_id is embedded in the output string ('Background subagent started with agent_id=<agent-id>.').
There is NO dedicated launch-acknowledgment event separate from PostToolUse; the launch IS the PostToolUse.
The background subagent's own tool calls may fire as hook events (sharing parent session_id) BEFORE the parent stops, but there is no completion hook when the subagent finishes asynchronously.

C05_backgroundCompletion.scenario: Background subagent terminal completion observed via read_subagent (block:true).

tool_input.task: <prompt: read sentinel and report first line>
tool_input.title: Read sentinel.txt first line

tool_input.task: <prompt: read sentinel and report first line>
tool_input.title: Read sentinel.txt first line

tool_response.output: Background subagent started with agent_id=<agent-id>. You can wait for this agent to finish using the read_subagent tool, otherwise you will automatically be notified with a <subagent_completion_notification> when it completes.
Subagent <agent-id> completed. Its full report is delivered in the <subagent_completion_notification> message; you do not need to read it again.

fieldObservations: read_subagent tool_input: {agent_id, block?, timeout?}. agent_id is the ONLY reliable correlation key to the launch.
Terminal completion is observable ONLY via read_subagent PostToolUse (success:true + 'completed' in output). There is NO dedicated completion hook event.

The async <subagent_completion_notification> is delivered to the AGENT'S CONTEXT, not as a hook event. If the parent relies on the notification instead of calling read_subagent, there is NO hook-observable completion.
This is the S09 STOP-gate evidence: a ledger incremented on background launch cannot be reliably cleared by a hook on completion.

C06_repeatedRead.scenario: read_subagent called twice on the same completed background subagent (first blocking, second non-blocking).

tool_response.output: Subagent <agent-id> completed. Its full report is delivered in the <subagent_completion_notification> message; you do not need to read it again.

fieldObservations: A REPEATED read_subagent on an already-completed subagent returns success:true AGAIN and re-serves the report. It is indistinguishable from the first terminal completion by hook payload alone.

Implication for S09: treating every read_subagent PostToolUse with success:true as a completion would DOUBLE-DECREMENT the ledger. A deduplication key (agent_id + observed-completion) is required, but in-memory sets do not survive separate adapter subprocess invocations.
The first (block:true) and second (no block) reads have DIFFERENT tool_use_ids but the SAME agent_id.

C07_cancel.scenario: ask_user_question in headless -p mode: the question is canceled before a human can answer (no interactive TTY).
fieldObservations: ask_user_question tool_input.questions[]: {question, header, options[]}. Each option: {label, description?}.
NO 'id' field on questions in this capture; NO 'multi_select' field when unset (field ABSENT, not false). The neutral spec field 'multiSelect' maps to native 'multi_select' (per S08).
A canceled question fires PreToolUse but NOT PostToolUse — the tool never completes. The agent is told 'It looks like you canceled the question.'
BLOCKED (C07 answered / C08 answered variants): headless -p cannot produce a human-answered PostToolUse. The answered output envelope was NOT captured. See capture-provenance.json BLOCKED rows.

C09_reviewerIdentity.scenario: A subagent dispatched with profile 'subagent_explore' performs a grep with glob_pattern. Probes whether any hook field identifies the dispatched reviewer profile on the child's tool calls.

tool_input.title: <title>
tool_input.task: <prompt: grep for searchable in md files>

tool_response.output: No matches found for pattern 'searchable' in <project-root>

tool_input.title: <title>
tool_input.task: <prompt: grep for searchable in md files>

tool_response.output:
Subagent agent_id=<agent-id> completed successfully:

<subagent report text>

fieldObservations: ESTABLISHED (negative result): the subagent's grep PreToolUse/PostToolUse carry NO profile, NO agent_type, NO agent_id field. They share the parent's session_id and prompt_id.
The ONLY hook-provided association to the dispatching profile is the parent's run_subagent tool_input.profile and the agent_id embedded in the run_subagent PostToolUse output string.
Once the subagent is running, its individual read/grep/glob/edit/write tool calls CANNOT be attributed to the reviewer profile from hook payload alone.
This is the S07 STOP-gate evidence: reliable reviewer identity is NOT available on child tool calls. The adapter's devin.agent_type/devin.agent_id assumptions are NOT backed by real payloads.
